Alicia / team — attaching a quick CSV (eval_prompts.csv) with representative prompt mix I used for the sims. Notes from the first pass:

- Baseline (no caching, small-batch): ~0.0018 USD per 1k tokens (hosted mid-sized model) => roughly $1.8 / 1M tokens.
- With prefix caching at 30% hit rate and 64-token batching we see ~25-32% improvement in tokens/$ depending on request shape.
- Prefetching for predictable flows (e.g., patient intake forms) reduces P95 slightly but increases burst CPU; needs rule-based TTLs.

Quick bullets for the MAP cost tab (what I'll add):
- Inputs: token mix (prompt/response), avg tokens per call, sessions/day (10k/50k), cache hit scenarios (0/30/60%).
- Outputs: tokens per USD, monthly run rate, projected delta vs current vendor (if we have their sample).
- Gating metrics: <15% variance between forecasted and observed tokens/$ during pilot week.

I'll drop updated sims by Tue EOD and include per-DAU tables.

Adding a short risks & acceptance section for the MAP workbook. Please incorporate into the gating checklist.

Risk items:
- Model variant fallback: if we route to a larger model during degraded capacity, tokens/$ may shift +60% — require auto-fallback cap and a "cost alarm" in the MAP.
- Quantization & precision: 4-bit quantized variants lower inference cost but may regress on hallucination for clinical language; include QA pass on a 50-sample eval set before we accept cheaper variant.

Suggested acceptance lines (to be yes/no gates at milestone):
- Pilot signoff: observed tokens/$ within ±20% of MAP baseline across pilot week AND no critical hallucination failures on eval set.
- SLA test: routing fallback does not trigger more than 5% of calls during a 24h window.
- Security gate: audit log sampling shows zero PII exfiltration and encryption-at-rest validated.

I'll add a short appendix with the 50-sample eval prompts and suggested pass/fail thresholds.

— Irene
Applied ML / Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
